peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates for BAC discuss nonperforming loans and accrued interest receivable, which are credit quality and asset valuation metrics, not collateral held to reimburse guarantee losses or indemnification risks as disclosed by Citi.

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm provides indemnifications and guarantees in its capacity as an agency lender and sponsoring member of the Fixed Income Clearing Corporation. Securities lending indemnifications had maximum payouts of $10.62 billion in December 2024 and minimal performance risk due to collateral requirements exceeding the value of lent securities.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Citi disclose collateral held specifically to reimburse losses under securities lending indemnifications. Citi reports $62.5 billion in securities and other marketable assets held as collateral, with the majority supporting securities lending indemnifications. GS reports $11.02 billion in collateral held in connection with securities lending indemnifications. Both firms manage counterparty risk in securities lending by holding collateral to cover market value shortfalls if borrowers fail to return securities. Citi's total securities collateral is significantly larger in absolute terms than GS's reported securities lending collateral.

sentences.text: Securities and other marketable assets held as collateral amounted to $62.5 billion and $67.7 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The majority of collateral is held to reimburse losses realized under securities lending indemnifications.
The maximum payout of such indemnifications was $10.62 billion as of December 2024 and $14.19 billion as of December 2023.
Collateral held by the lenders in connection with securities lending indemnifications was $11.02 billion as of December 2024 and $14.63 billion as of December 2023.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, net derivatives receivable included $51.9 billion and $48.3 billion of netted cash collateral, while net derivatives payable included $60.8 billion and $70.0 billion, respectively; this collateral relates to OTC and OTC-cleared instruments.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) disclose significant holdings of cash collateral related to their financial operations. Citi held $49.0 billion in cash collateral available to reimburse losses realized under guarantees and indemnifications. JPM reports that its net derivatives receivable included $51.9 billion of netted cash collateral, and net derivatives payable included $60.8 billion of netted cash collateral. Both firms manage substantial cash collateral positions to mitigate credit risk in their respective indemnification and derivative activities, with Citi framing it as collateral held to reimburse guarantee losses and JPM framing it as cash collateral netted in derivative balances.

sentences.text: Cash collateral available to Citi to reimburse losses realized under these guarantees and indemnifications amounted to $49.0 billion and $52.5 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

comparisons.peer_topic: Letters of Credit and Financial Guarantees
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm has outstanding letters of credit and financial guarantees issued by third-party banks, for which it is contingently liable, primarily used to provide collateral for securities/commodities trading and to satisfy margin requirements.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Morgan Stanley (MS) disclose the use of letters of credit as collateral to support trading obligations. Citi held $3.1 billion in letters of credit held as collateral at December 31, 2024. MS states that its outstanding letters of credit and other financial guarantees are primarily used to provide collateral for securities and commodities trading and to satisfy margin requirements. While MS focuses on the contingently liability aspect of issuing these letters to counterparties, Citi focuses on holding them as collateral to reimburse guarantee losses, indicating a shared business driver of using letters of credit for collateral purposes in trading activities.

sentences.text: In addition, letters of credit in favor of Citi held as collateral amounted to $3.1 billion and $3.1 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The Firm has outstanding letters of credit and other financial guarantees issued by third-party banks to certain of the Firm's counterparties.

The Firm is contingently liable for these letters of credit and other financial guarantees, which are primarily used to provide collateral for securities and commodities traded and to satisfy various margin requirements in lieu of depositing cash or securities with these counterparties.
